title: Observer’s guide for ISO 2026-W08
planetary_coordinate: geocentric tropical ecliptic longitude; Monday 00:00 UTC

planet_relations.basis: Star Almanack preserved geocentric tropical ecliptic longitude

note:
ISO 2026-W08 runs from February 16 through February 22. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 0.4° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌑 New Moon — 12:01:09 UTC. The dark Moon favors faint targets and extended star fields. Use Adhara, Wezen as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 0.4° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified for binocular observing this week.

**Small telescope:** Concentrate on M50. Increase magnification only after the target and surrounding pattern are secure.

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.
